findings.finding: The cutover runs pass-by-pass over the ~1509 existing bindings (each description re-emits 'exactly once'), so a rollout aborted mid-migration leaves a MIXED population — some bindings with rich-canonical baselines/rich_sha, some still plain — but the plan does not state how that partially-migrated set is handled on rollback or on resume.
findings.location: The live cutover (both clients) 'Each already-synced description re-emits exactly once … then converges'; Approach; Testing 'Rollback'
scenarios: Cutover flag enabled; roughly half the bindings re-emit to rich and get rich baselines over several passes; the flag is turned off before the rest are reached; the store now holds a mix of rich and plain baselines and the plan does not define which the restored plain compare path trusts, risking divergent/echoing behavior across the two cohorts.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify and test the post-rollback interpreted state: after the cutover flag is turned off, assert that baselines/rich_sha written during the cutover window do not read as divergence under the restored plain path (compensate-forward by re-normalizing or clearing the rich baselines on rollback), not merely that the outbound wire reverts to plain.

Plan: the three-way diff routes every side through codec normalize_outbound; on rollback that reverts to the plain path, but the at-rest baselines remain rich-canonical.
Rollback AC/test asserts only 'the wire reverts to the plain/identity encode for that client' — silent on residual baseline / rich_sha interpretation after the flag flips off.
binding_store.py:104: 'An absent baseline (including v1) is valid and degrades to local-wins' confirms baseline interpretation is load-bearing for the sync decision.
Post-rollback applicability trigger met: the plan 'changes how existing persisted records are interpreted' and 'performs a one-way transformation'.
findings.finding: The cutover rewrites persisted baselines to rich-canonical post-push form and re-emits every synced description once (a one-way transform), but the rollback only asserts the WIRE reverts to plain/identity — it does not assert on the post-rollback interpreted state of the baselines and rich_sha entries written during the cutover window.
findings.location: Approach (post-push baseline merge into ctx.curr_snapshot); AC 'The cutover is flag-gated and reverts to the plain/identity wire when off'; Testing 'Rollback' (test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain)
scenarios: Cutover enabled; several descriptions re-emit and their baselines are stored rich-canonical; a bad rollout flips the flag off; the next pass compares a rich-canonical baseline against a plain-normalized remote, sees a false divergence, and re-syncs (echoes) a body no one changed — or misreads it as a human edit and clobbers it.
findings.suggested_fix: On rollback, either (a) re-normalize the stored baseline back through the plain codec so the restored compare path sees equality, or (b) treat a rich-shaped baseline as 'absent' (degrade-to-local-wins per binding_store.py:104) so no spurious divergence fires; add a test asserting a no-edit binding emits zero outbound after the flag is turned off.
